source.title: Planning and acting in partially observable stochastic domains

confidence_rationale: The foundational formal statement of the exact problem INF-7/ARC-091 names: under partial observability the policy must map a BELIEF over hidden states (not the raw observation) to action. High source-quality (the canonical POMDP reference) and a precise normative grounding for MECH-385. Confidence capped because REE explicitly does NOT adopt exact Bayesian belief updating, so the mapping is principle-level, with real divergence in mechanism.
failure_signatures: Failure-to-infer-hidden-danger / hidden-safety is exactly the cost of acting on observation rather than belief; the POMDP framework makes precise why an observation->action policy is provably suboptimal when state is hidden.
Context loss (MECH-126): a memoryless reactive policy that ignores observation/action history is the degenerate belief-state failure the formalism rules out.

mapping.source_claim_statement: In a partially observable Markov decision process the agent cannot observe the true state and must maintain a belief state -- a probability distribution over hidden states -- updated from its action/observation history; the optimal policy is a function of the belief state (equivalently the history), not of the current observation.
mapping.ree_translation: The formal backbone of MECH-385 (belief-state hypothesis set) and the ARC-091 thesis that E3 must select trajectories over inferred state, not raw observation. REE's bounded top-k hypothesis set with confidence weights is a tractable, non-Bayesian approximation of the POMDP belief state; this paper supplies the why (observation->action is provably insufficient under hidden state).
mapping.mapping_caveat: REE deliberately avoids the full POMDP formalism: it keeps a bounded set of competing hypotheses with heuristic precision rather than an exact posterior, separates harm/goal/residue streams instead of a single reward, and never commits to closed-form belief updates. So this grounds the PROBLEM and the necessity of belief-over-observation, not REE's specific solution; importing POMDP optimality guarantees into REE would be a category error.
mapping.source_context: Theoretical AI / operations-research formalism; tabular discrete state-action POMDPs with offline value-iteration solution methods.

confidence_components.notes: Canonical source. Mapping fidelity moderate: it nails the problem statement (belief not observation) but REE's approximate, stream-separated solution diverges from exact POMDP machinery -- hence the higher transfer risk.
